stance.quote:
a series of life-threatening problems within many of the world’s great financial
institutions was unveiled

summary: In 2008 the credit crisis froze credit markets, and falling home and stock prices set off a freefall in business activity.
Clayton's lending is threatened by the credit crisis because government-backed funders borrow far more cheaply than Berkshire.

stance.quote: The investment world has gone from underpricing risk to overpricing it.

summary: Investors moved from underpricing to overpricing risk, and the late-2008 Treasury bond bubble is compared with the Internet and housing bubbles.
Berkshire's credit-default contracts paid $2.5 billion of losses in the financial panic yet should end with an underwriting profit and free float.

stance.quote: That’s what allowed us to invest $15.6 billion in 25 days of panic following the Lehman bankruptcy in 2008.

summary: Financial strength let Berkshire invest $15.6 billion in the 25 days of panic after the Lehman bankruptcy in 2008.

stance.quote:
the more you know about derivatives, the less you
will feel you can learn from the disclosures normally proffered you

summary: Derivatives disclosures reveal little about a dealer's risks, and Freddie Mac's accounting shows why investors should be suspicious.
The repeal of the General Utilities Doctrine lowers what shareholders of oil and gas, media and real estate companies can realize on a sale.
Aggressive real estate operators, corporate acquirers and oil drillers saw their fortunes disappear while patient investors kept theirs.

stance.quote:
We will continue to ignore political and economic forecasts,
which are an expensive distraction for many investors and
businessmen.

summary: Berkshire ignores economic forecasts, since the Vietnam War, two oil shocks and wide Treasury yield swings were unforeseeable.
Berkshire holds four convertible preferreds worth about cost, except Gillette slightly above and USAir substantially below.

stance.quote: your Chairman displayed exquisite timing: I plunged into the business at almost the exact moment that it ran into severe problems.

summary: USAir ran into severe problems just after Berkshire bought in, from industry conditions and the troubled Piedmont merger.

stance.quote: In a business selling a commodity-type product, it's impossible to be a lot smarter than your dumbest competitor.

summary: Airline economics deteriorated since the purchase because of kamikaze pricing by some carriers in a commodity business.

stance.quote: our investment is now less secure than at the time I made it

summary: Unless the industry is decimated, USAir should work out all right, though the investment is less secure than when made.

stance.quote:
We are delighted to be in partnership
with them.

summary: The Blumkin family runs Nebraska Furniture Mart with great buying skill, work ethic and character.
A five-person head office outproduces larger corporate groups, and Munger and Buffett run the business by telephone.

stance.quote: inflation acts as a gigantic corporate tapeworm.

summary: Inflation consumes investment dollars for receivables, inventory and fixed assets, hurting the least prosperous companies most.
Net worth gained 19.5% in 1987 and book value per share compounded at 23.1% since 1964; business value matters more than book.
Bank ownership carries earthquake, systemic financial-panic and West Coast real estate risks, and Wells Fargo is seen as vulnerable.
Insurance did well overall in the decade despite mistakes in surety, urban auto, aviation fronting and California workers' compensation.
High trading volume is a curse for owners since the chair-changing tax of costs could reach about $7.5 billion.
